doc: F2 - F1 of Worley3 at (points @ rot^T) * 8, 512 unit directions, seed 3: 0 on a cell border, rising into each cell. The Worley tables (plan0) and the rotation (plan1) are inputs; the worley_seed the seed draws is only recorded. Output float32, shape = points.shape[:-1]. Chained float32 (matmul, scale, 27-neighbor search): recomputed in float64, with the matmul in both orders and with the points nudged by one float32 ulp either way: the largest observed difference is 2e-06 (it grows with the frequency because q is quantized to float32); tolerance rtol 1e-5 + atol 2e-05 (10x). The Python casts the points to float32 first; that cast is not enforced (the tolerance was measured with float64 recomputes, so a float64 pipeline passes). The Python evaluates in chunks of 1 << 20 points: a port may chunk differently (checked at build time with chunks of 7 and 97 points: the same field within this tolerance). The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
